correctness.rationale: For the precisely enumerated seven-vertex graph, the standalone verifier reconstructs all eighteen closed sets, 38 poset edges, sixteen triangles and their free involution. The eight recorded orbit pairs are each verified free at the removal stage and leave a connected 18-vertex 22-edge graph with a free involution and no invariant edge. The index-one conclusion follows since a connected free one-dimensional Z2-CW complex admits an equivariant map to S1 but not S0; the box/Lovász equivalence is established in arXiv:math/0310339. Direct exhaustive coloring verifies chromatic number four. No finite-to-infinite extrapolation occurs.

value.rationale: The box-complex Z2-index is a canonical obstruction introduced specifically to bound chromatic number. The smallest classical unit-distance four-chromatic witness (Moser spindle) is a motivated test case for the strength of this invariant. An explicit free equivariant collapse proves the bound misses one full color despite the graph having squares that escape the standard no-K22 index-one theorem; the quotient graph and orbit certificate explain the failure structurally. This exact invariant is not implied by ordinary homology and may guide analysis of Hajós joins, rather than being an arbitrary small count.
